entries.title: Isaiah 28:1
segments: To the drunkards of Ephraim; rather, "of the drunkards of Ephraim;" and so in

. 
 
  Which are on the head; for "are," which is supplied by the translators, we may better put "is," making the clause refer to the "glorious beauty" of "the drunkards of Ephraim," is Samaria, the capital of the kingdom of Israel.  This city was "on the head of the fat valleys" of these drunkards, as it lay on the summit of a hill surrounded by fertile valleys. 
 
vv 1,3,7. 
 
Crimes and abuses of every kind follow in the train of drunkenness. When the rulers of a people are addicted to this sin, they will pervert truth and righteousness, and bring upon themselves and their country the just judgments of God.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:2
segments:
A mighty and strong one; a mighty conqueror whom he will send against Samaria. 
 
  With the hand; with a violent hand.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:4
segments: Hasty fruit; the early figs, which were esteemed a great delicacy.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:5
segments: Unto the residue of his people; while Ephraim's "crown of pride" is destroyed, God will be himself "a crown of glory" and "a diadem of beauty," to the remnant of his people in Jerusalem.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:6
segments: To the gate; back to the gate of the enemy.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:7
segments: But they also have erred; the people of Judah, as well as of Ephraim.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:9
segments:
vv 9-10. 
 
  Whom shall he teach--there a little; it is generally agreed that these are the scoffing words of the Jews, complaining that the prophet multiplies his precepts to them as if they were babes.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:11
segments: With stammering lips; this is God's answer to the scoffers.  Since they stammer, that is, scoff at the prophet's message, God will teach them by stammering lips, that is, by giving them up to the power of stammering foreigners.  In the Hebrew, to stammer, to scoff, and to speak in a foreign tongue, are all expressed by the same verb.  Compare

entries.title: Isaiah 28:12
segments: This is the rest; faith in God and obedience to his law.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:13
segments: The word of the Lord was unto them; God has indeed multiplied his precepts to them as to children, but with no other result than their increased wickedness and more aggravated ruin. Compare

entries.title: Isaiah 28:15
segments:
Covenant with death--with hell--at agreement; the covenant is, that death and hell shall not injure them.  This they say not in word, but in spirit and action.  They are confident that their lying devices will save them. 
 
In nothing does the desperate wickedness of men more clearly manifest itself than in the delusions which they practise upon themselves in respect to escaping the punishment of their sins.  Every transgressor has some "refuge of lies" in which he hopes to be saved, though he neglects the only way of salvation which God has provided for him.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:16
segments:
A sure foundation; the Messiah, who is here contrasted with the vain refuges of these scoffers. 
 
  Make haste; flee in terror, as the wicked must from their refuges of lies.

vv 16-20. 
 
Jesus Christ is the one foundation which God has laid in Zion for sinners.  They who build upon him their hopes for eternity shall never be put to shame; but the hail and tempest of the last day shall sweep away every hiding-place of man's invention.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:17
segments: Judgment--to the line--righteousness to the plummet; proceed with exact justice, not sparing the guilty.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:19
segments: From the time that it goeth forth; or, "as often as it," the scourge, "passeth over."

entries.title: Isaiah 28:20
segments: The bed--the covering; their lying devices, to which they trusted for deliverance.

, or to

  Strange; unheard of, extraordinary.  What the "strange work" is,

entries.title: Isaiah 28:22
segments:
The whole earth; the whole land of Judea.  The original word means both "earth" and "land." 
 
They who scoff at God's judgments will soon find themselves entangled in them, with no power either to escape or endure them.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:24
segments:
vv 24-28. 
 
  Doth the ploughman plough--bruise it with his horsemen; the husbandman does not always plough, he also sows; his different seeds he arranges each in the right place; in threshing he pursues different modes according to the nature of the grain: much more, then, must God, who gives to the husbandman all his skill, adapt his dealings with men to their different characters and circumstances, as the case may demand.  The interference from this is, that the righteous will be finally saved, and the incorrigibly wicked in due time destroyed.

entries.title: Isaiah 28:29
segments: This also; this wisdom of the husbandman.  How much deeper, then, must be the wisdom of God himself.
